definition: WBIS usually refers to the Modified Weight Bias Internalization Scale, a 10-item self-report measure of internalized weight stigma. It assesses the extent to which a person applies negative weight-related stereotypes to themselves, linked with self-devaluation and poorer body image, eating-related difficulties, and lower self-esteem.

reasons: The packet supports that WBIS-M is the Modified Weight Bias Internalization Scale and that it is a 10-item measure, but it does not explicitly state that the scale “applies negative weight-related stereotypes to themselves.” The packet instead describes internalized weight stigma as “self-stigmatization, leading to self-devaluation,” without specifying “negative weight-related stereotypes.”
The phrase “WBIS usually refers to” is not supported by the packet, which only mentions “Modified Weight Bias Internalization Scale (WBIS-M)” in the context of an adaptation/validation study.
The packet supports the Modified Weight Bias Internalization Scale (WBIS-M), but the definition identifies WBIS without the -M; that acronym/sense mismatch is not established by the source.

The source supports validity/reliability and associations with body dissatisfaction, restrictive/compensatory behaviors, food/weight concerns, binge eating severity, and self-esteem, but it does not support the broader wording about ‘eating-related difficulties’ or ‘poorer body image’ as a general definition of WBIS rather than findings from one study.
